titleBlock.headline: Multi-omic analysis of biological aging biomarkers in long-term calorie restriction and endurance exercise practitioners
titleBlock.authors: Fiorito, G., Tosti, V., Polidoro, S., Bertozzi, B., Veronese, N., Cava, E., Spelta, F., Piccio, L., Early, D.S., Raftery, D., Vineis, P. & Fontana, L.

keyTakeaway: Long-term calorie restriction (CR) and endurance exercise (EX) are not biologically redundant: CR preferentially lowers systemic clinical blood PhenoAge acceleration (-2.96 years) and remodels circulating hormones, plasma metabolomics, and gut microbiota, whereas endurance exercise uniquely reduces colon mucosal Horvath epigenetic age (-2.25 years) and stochastic epigenetic mutation load (-4.91 years).

studyOverview.label: Participants
studyOverview.value: Full blood cohort (n = 117): 41 long-term CR practitioners, 41 master endurance athletes (EX), and 35 age-matched Western Diet (WD) controls; plus a 6-layer multi-omic biopsy sub-cohort (n = 41: 12 CR, 11 EX, 12 WD, 6 young WD).

studyOverview.label: Methodology
studyOverview.value: Clinical blood Levine PhenoAge (9 biomarkers) in n = 117, paired with 6-layer multi-omics (phenoBioAge, fecal 16S rRNA microbiomeBioAge, plasma metabolomeBioAge, circulating hormoneBioAge, sigmoid colon mucosa 450K DNAmBioAge, and colon RNA-seq transcriptomeBioAge) in n = 41.

studyOverview.label: Primary Finding
studyOverview.value: CR reduced clinical blood PhenoAge acceleration by -2.96 years (p = 0.003), while EX reduced colon mucosa Horvath DNAm age by -2.25 years (p = 0.04) and colon epigenetic mutation load by -4.91 years (p = 0.003).

scorecardOverview.title: The Question
scorecardOverview.content: Do long-term calorie restriction (CR) and chronic endurance exercise (EX) slow human biological aging through the same molecular pathways—or do they target distinct tissues and omic layers?

scorecardOverview.title: The Methodology
scorecardOverview.content: Investigated 117 humans (41 CR, 41 EX, 35 WD) for clinical blood PhenoAge, and performed 6-layer multi-omic biological age profiling (blood phenoBioAge, fecal microbiomeBioAge, plasma metabolomeBioAge, circulating hormoneBioAge, colon mucosa DNAmBioAge, and colon transcriptomeBioAge) in a 41-subject subset.

scorecardOverview.title: The Breakthrough
scorecardOverview.content: Diet and exercise act on complementary axes: CR significantly lowered systemic blood PhenoAge (-2.96 yr, p = 0.003) and reshaped hormonal/metabolomic/microbiome signatures, whereas EX uniquely rejuvenated colon tissue epigenetic clocks (-2.25 yr Horvath DNAmAA; -4.91 yr Epigenetic Mutation Load).

multiOmics.title: Colon DNA Methylation
multiOmics.desc: Illumina HumanMethylation450 (450K) BeadChip array on sigmoid colon mucosa biopsies measuring Horvath DNAmAA, DNAmBioAge, and stochastic Epigenetic Mutation Load (EML).

multiOmics.title: Colon Transcriptomics
multiOmics.desc: RNA-seq of colon mucosa (transcriptomeBioAge) identifying focal adhesion, ECM remodeling, and basal transcription shifts.

multiOmics.title: Blood PhenoAge & Hormones
multiOmics.desc: Systemic clinical blood chemistry (Levine PhenoAge / phenoBioAge) paired with circulating endocrine/metabolic hormone profiling (hormoneBioAge).

multiOmics.title: Plasma Metabolome & Microbiome
multiOmics.desc: Plasma metabolomics (metabolomeBioAge) and 16S rRNA fecal metagenomics (microbiomeBioAge) mapping host-microbe co-metabolism.

clockBenchmarks.name: Colon Epigenetic Mutation Load (EML_AA)
clockBenchmarks.subtitle: Stochastic epigenetic drift (log2 epigenetic mutations age acceleration vs. Western Diet)
clockBenchmarks.footnote: In sensitivity analyses (Section 3.3), EX practitioners exhibited a -4.91 yr reduction in colon EML age acceleration vs. WD (p = 0.003) and -4.04 yr vs. CR (p = 0.02), whereas CR vs. WD was not statistically significant.

clockBenchmarks.name: Clinical Blood PhenoAge Acceleration (PhenoAA)
clockBenchmarks.subtitle: Levine 9-biomarker clinical chemistry & hematological biological age acceleration
clockBenchmarks.footnote: CR practitioners showed a statistically significant -2.96 yr reduction in clinical blood PhenoAge acceleration vs. WD (p = 0.003), driven by lower CRP, glucose, white blood cell count, and alkaline phosphatase, whereas EX vs. WD did not reach statistical significance.

clockBenchmarks.name: Colon Horvath Epigenetic Clock (DNAmAA)
clockBenchmarks.subtitle: Pan-tissue CpG methylation age acceleration in intestinal epithelium
clockBenchmarks.footnote: Endurance athletes demonstrated a significant -2.25 yr reduction in colon mucosa Horvath epigenetic age acceleration compared to sedentary Western Diet controls (p = 0.04), whereas CR vs. WD was not statistically significant.

cr.title: Calorie Restriction (Diet)
cr.primaryMechanism: Systemic metabolic efficiency, endocrine/hormonal optimization, plasma metabolome remodeling, and gut microbiome shifts.
cr.biomarkersImproved: Significantly reduced clinical blood PhenoAge (-2.96 yr, p = 0.003), lowered insulin/IGF-1 and systemic inflammation (hs-CRP), and favorably remodeled plasma metabolites and gut microbiota.

ex.title: Endurance Exercise
ex.primaryMechanism: Tissue-level epigenetic maintenance, reduced stochastic DNAm drift, and colon mucosal protection.
ex.biomarkersImproved: Significantly reduced colon mucosa Horvath DNAm age (-2.25 yr, p = 0.04) and stochastic Epigenetic Mutation Load (-4.91 yr, p = 0.003), while upregulating mitochondrial oxidative defense and ECM integrity.

sharedMechanisms: While distinct in their primary tissue and omic signatures, both CR and EX converged on shared youthful features compared to Western Diet controls: attenuated oxidative stress, down-regulated basal transcriptional noise, and improved cardiometabolic risk profiles.
conclusions: Calorie restriction and endurance exercise are not biologically redundant; they decelerate human aging through parallel, complementary molecular pathways.
Calorie restriction predominantly improves systemic blood clinical chemistry (PhenoAA -2.96 yr), circulating hormones, plasma metabolomics, and gut microbiome architecture.
Endurance exercise uniquely preserves tissue-level epigenetic fidelity in colon mucosa, reducing Horvath DNAm age (-2.25 yr) and stochastic epigenetic mutation load (-4.91 yr).

structuredConclusions.title: Distinct Clocks Respond to Diet vs. Exercise
structuredConclusions.content: Clinical blood PhenoAge responded strongly to long-term Calorie Restriction (-2.96 years, p = 0.003), whereas tissue-level colon epigenetic clocks (Horvath DNAmAA -2.25 years; Epigenetic Mutation Load -4.91 years) responded specifically to Endurance Exercise.

structuredConclusions.title: Complementary 6-Omic Remodeling
structuredConclusions.content: Multi-omic integration across colon biopsies, blood, and stool showed that CR primarily reshapes systemic blood chemistry, hormones, plasma metabolites, and gut microbial taxa, while EX stabilizes mucosal DNA methylation and extracellular matrix transcription.

structuredConclusions.title: Synergistic Longevity Architecture
structuredConclusions.content: Because neither intervention alone captured all youthful molecular signatures observed in young controls, combining nutritional moderation with aerobic exercise is required for comprehensive systemic and tissue-level rejuvenation.

protocolRecommendations: Do not treat nutrition and exercise as interchangeable: combine caloric/nutritional quality optimization with regular endurance training to capture both systemic metabolic and tissue-epigenetic rejuvenation.
Target the Calorie Restriction axis via nutrient-dense, anti-inflammatory dietary patterns that lower fasting insulin/glucose, hs-CRP, and support metabolic and microbiome health.
Target the Endurance Exercise axis via consistent aerobic conditioning to suppress stochastic epigenetic mutation load (EML) and preserve mucosal tissue integrity.
